_comment: The Discovery deliverable: one comparison basis, the candidates compared against it, the exclusion log, and the outcome. Save it as JSON and run scripts/check_shortlist_consistency.py before presenting anything. Until this template existed there was no container contract at all -- candidates[] was a shape the checks assumed and nothing asked the author to produce, which makes a gate opt-in on the very declaration a defect hides behind.

_enums._comment: The checker reads its vocabularies from here, so adding a state is a contract edit rather than a code edit, and the checker cannot drift from the document that describes it.

trip_context._comment: The single comparison basis. Every candidate's figure is measured against this, which is what makes two numbers rankable at all.

outcome._comment: Required on every Discovery artifact. Omitting it used to be the escape from every rule keyed on it. 'shortlist' means candidates survived and are ranked; 'constraint_conflict' means nothing survived and the traveller must relax something; 'blocked' means the question could not be answered and blocking_fact says what went unverified -- an unfinished filter and a real conflict produce the same empty pass set, and the traveller should not be asked to give up a real requirement to escape the difference.

excluded._comment: The one-line exclusion log. Deliberately thinner than a candidate record: a rejected destination was never researched to candidate depth, and demanding that it were would buy research the budget forbids.

conditional_options._comment: SKILL.md's 'possible if X changes'. A conditional is an offer, never a recommendation, so these stay out of recommendation.winner regardless of how well they score.
